terminus.finding: Zhang Rongzhe's 2019 Nuannuan fall-prevention work-team draft argues that residents may possess abilities such as oral history or storytelling without recognizing them as valuable; the exchange mechanism and work team help identify and realize that value. It also distinguishes a decentralized time-bank model from a work-team model in which exchange and credit creation are concentrated in a central intermediary.
terminus.generated: The previous scale/carrier model needs a second gate: capability can be portable yet socially inert if nobody can recognize, translate and validate it as exchangeable or usable. MUTHER therefore separates portability from legibility. Capability migration requires not only a carrier that can move, but an interface that makes the moved capacity recognizable to a new network. The same interface can enable recognition while also concentrating gatekeeping power.
terminus.relationToPrevious: Revises the Lee Tung Street capacity-migration finding. Transfer is not guaranteed by possession of skill or movement experience alone; transfer also depends on a recognition/translation interface. This adds a mechanism to the earlier local-vs-transferable capacity distinction.
terminus.next: seek a case where highly portable expertise fails to transfer because the receiving system cannot recognize or credential it, and a counterexample where recognition happens without a central gatekeeper
